<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix canonical tiering storage sizing when TP exceeds the number of KV heads, so replicated GQA caches can be persisted and reused across TP sizes. Discovered during the chunked-local work in #61886 and reproduced independently with full attention.

Follow-up: #62162 enables chunked-local canonical offload on top of this fix.

## Claims

- Canonical storage counts unique KV-head copies rather than physical TP ranks.
- Worker mmap population stays within the deduplicated row.
- Default CPU offloading, noncanonical layouts and existing MLA replication semantics are preserved.

## Validation

Tested fix commit `a99a46153a` independently of the chunked-local change.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py
```

**135 passed.** Regression cases cover KV heads 1/2/4, TP 1/2/4, canonical on/off, row size, capacity, namespace and last-rank mmap bounds. Pre-commit passed.

On **2× RTX 5090**, a deterministic tiny Llama4 full-attention control (1 KV head, FP16, eager, Triton) passed all **5 inference processes**: no-offload TP1 reference and independent TP1→TP2 / TP2→TP1 filesystem producer-reader pairs.

| Direction | Cold/reload cache-hit contexts | Maximum absolute logprob delta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP1 → TP2 | 240/240 in each phase | 0.001477 |
| TP2 → TP1 | 240/240 in each phase | 0.002874 |

Compared all 512 vocabulary entries at 240 fixed contexts against the no-offload reference, tolerance 0.005. Filesystem reads and CPU→GPU transfer counters confirm actual reuse after restart and GPU-cache reset.

[Commands, CPU logs, numerical/transfer results, environment and source hashes](https://github.com/xiaoba17/vllm/tree/10218a6806b5fff79919eb02fff11c265d2c41de). GPU validation was performed outside CI; the archived harness uses host-specific paths, documented in its README. These are execution-correctness tests with random tiny weights, not model-quality or performance benchmarks.

## Details

Canonical mappings already deduplicate replicated GQA heads, but tiering allocated rows using physical world size. With one KV head, TP1 and TP2 therefore shared a storage namespace while expecting different file sizes (4096 versus 8192 bytes in the minimal Linux reproducer), causing the TP2 reader to reject TP1 files.

Carry the certified canonical replication factor into tiering's copy-count calculation and map population ranks to unique head slots. The canonical mapping's rank and writer-selection logic remains unchanged. Regression mutations removing either the sizing correction or the rank correction fail the targeted tests.

Duplicate-work check: #56953 concerns per-group slot sizing, whereas this fixes replicated TP copies; #60782 refactors shared-region classes without changing their sizing semantics. Neither implements this fix. Related tracking issue: #61886 (not closed by this PR).

The GPU/native-extension baseline is `8e25bbca19`; latest-main mergeability was checked separately, not presented as a new GPU run.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and PR preparation. I have reviewed the changes and completed the relevant tests and behavioral validation.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

</details>

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("total_kv_heads", [1, 2, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp_size", [1, 2, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("canonical", [False, True])
+def test_canonical_gqa_file_size_matches_across_tp(total_kv_heads, tp_size, canonical):
+    """A shared file namespace must not grow when TP replicates KV heads."""
+    config = _make_vllm_config(
+        tensor_parallel_size=tp_size,
+        extra_config={"canonical_layout": canonical, "cpu_bytes_to_use": 1 << 20},
+    )
+    config.model_config.get_total_num_kv_heads.return_value = total_kv_heads
+    config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout = "LBNHC"
+    config.parallel_config.distributed_executor_backend = "mp"
+    cache_spec = FullAttentionSpec(
+        block_size=16,
+        num_kv_heads=max(1, total_kv_heads // tp_size),
+        head_size=128,
+        dtype=torch.float16,
+    )
+    kv_config = KVCacheConfig(
+        num_blocks=16,
+        kv_cache_tensors=[],
+        kv_cache_groups=[KVCacheGroupSpec(["layer"], cache_spec)],
+    )
+    off_config = build_offloading_config(config, kv_config)
+    off = TieringOffloadingSpec(off_config)
+    replicas = max(1, tp_size // total_kv_heads) if canonical else 1
+    assert off_config.canonical_kv_replicas == replicas
+    expected_bytes = 8192 * (
+        total_kv_heads if canonical else max(total_kv_heads, tp_size)
+    )
+    expected_bytes = round_up(expected_bytes, off.BLOCK_SIZE_ALIGNMENT)
+    assert off.kv_bytes_per_chunk == expected_bytes
+    assert off.num_chunks == (1 << 20) // expected_bytes
+    assert off.cpu_page_size_per_worker == cache_spec.page_size_bytes
+    if canonical:
+        mapper = FileMapper.from_offloading_spec("/cache", off, parallel_agnostic=True)
+        assert mapper.get_run_config()["tp_size"] == 1
+        # The last rank's prefault slot must fit even when replicas share a row.
+        off.config = replace(
+            off_config, parallel=replace(off_config.parallel, rank=tp_size - 1)
+        )
+        module = "vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.spec"
+        with (
+            patch(f"{module}.SharedOffloadRegion") as region,
+            patch(f"{module}.CPUOffloadingWorker"),
+        ):
+            off.create_worker(CanonicalKVCaches([], []))
+        args = region.call_args.kwargs
+        assert (args["rank"] + 1) * args["cpu_page_size"] <= args["kv_bytes_per_chunk"]
+
